newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Vanguard mulls T$200 bln wafer project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Vanguard mulls T$200 bln wafer project.

text.p: Vanguard International Semiconductor Corp, an affiliate of microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp, said on Wednesday it may invest T$200 billion to build two computer wafer plants.
The fabrication plants would be built in Taiwan's main high-tech park in northern Hsinchu, and likely would produce both eight-inch and 12-inch wafers, a Vanguard spokesman said by telephone.
But he said the project was still in the initial planning stage.
"This is a project we've been thinking about and feel it may be feasible, but we have not made a final decision," he said.
Vanguard said it would issue a more concrete proposal on the project at the end of 1997.

While huge at T$200 billion (US$7 billion), the Vanguard plan is dwarfed by 10-year projects unveiled recently by its flagship company Taiwan Semiconductor, Taiwan's largest chipmaker, and No.2 maker United Microelectronics.
Taiwan semiconductor said in April it would spend T$400 billion to build six advanced production lines in the new Tainan park, the biggest single investment in Taiwan to date.
Arch rival United Micro went Taiwan Semicon one better in June, announcing a T$500 billion project to build 12-inch wafer fabs at Tainan.

Similarly advanced multibillion-dollar projects have been announced by Winbond Electronics Corp ; Nan Ya Technology, the chipmaking unit of Nan Ya Plastics ; Macronix International ; Powerchip Co, a joint venture of Umax-Elite group and Mitsubishi Electric of Japan.
Vanguard is owned 27.52 percent by Taiwan Semiconductor.
